newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi paper says Iran blocking normalisation.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi paper says Iran blocking normalisation.

text.p: An Iraqi official newspaper on Wednesday said Iran was ignoring Baghdad's desire to normalise relations.

"Iraq is keen to improve and normalise its ties with Iran in the interest of the two countries...It is proved to us that Iran does not want to do so despite Iraq's goodwill gestures," al-Thawra said in a frontpage editorial by editor-in-chief Sami Mahdi.
The organ of the ruling Baath party accused Iran of delaying a visit by its foreign minister that it said had been agreed by the two countries.
Iraq and Iran fought a bitter war from 1980 to 1988. Iraq is still seeking the freedom of thousands of prisoners of war it says are held by Iran.
Iraq also blamed Iran for the attempted assassination of President Saddam Hussein's son Uday on December 12. Tehran denied the charge.
"Iran is still delaying a solution to the prisoners of war issue and interfering in Iraq's internal affairs," al-Thawra said.

Iran in turn has been angered by Iraq's sheltering of an Iranian opposition group. Last week Iraq accused Iranian agents of firing mortar bombs at the Baghdad headquarters of the Iranian Mujahideen Khalq.
